players.product: DDR5 RCD / DB, MRDIMM MRCD / MDB, CXL memory-expander controllers and PCIe retimers

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): H1 2026 revenue was RMB 33.35 hundred million, up 26.7% year over year; interconnect-chip revenue RMB 31.11 hundred million, up 26.4%; the four new interconnect products (MRCD/MDB, PCIe Retimer, CKD and CXL MXC) together RMB 5.38 hundred million, up 80.7%. Net profit attributable to shareholders RMB 19.97 hundred million, up 72.3%. Gross margin 65.3%, up 4.87 percentage points; interconnect-chip gross margin 69.3%, up 4.95 points. Q2 2026 revenue RMB 18.75 hundred million, up 32.8% year over year and 28.3% quarter over quarter; Q2 interconnect-chip revenue RMB 16.94 hundred million, up 28.2% year over year and 19.5% quarter over quarter, with a 67.4% product-line gross margin; Q2 revenue, interconnect revenue and net profit were single-quarter records.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 revenue RMB 33.35 hundred million (+26.7%); new products RMB 5.38 hundred million (+80.7%); GM 65.3%; Q2 revenue RMB 18.75 hundred million (+32.8% YoY, +28.3% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): DDR5 RCD demand grew markedly in H1 2026; third- and fourth-sub-generation RCDs together exceeded 50% of shipments and the fifth sub-generation began volume shipments. In June 2026 the company sampled its sixth-sub-generation DDR5 RCD supporting up to 9200MT/s and began pre-research on first-generation DDR6 memory-interconnect products. Its second-generation MRCD/MDB (12800MT/s) was in large-scale trial use in H1 with shipments rising significantly; management says MRDIMM volume ramp awaits next year's mass shipment of the new-generation CPUs that support second-generation MRDIMM, and its penetration pace has no historical pattern to go by. CKD chips (up to 9200MT/s) continued to ship.
quarterly_data.figure: 3rd+4th sub-gen RCD >50% of shipments; 6th sub-gen RCD sampled at 9200MT/s; MRCD/MDB gen 2 at 12800MT/s in large-scale trial

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): Montage is one of two vendors mainly supplying PCIe 5.0 Retimer chips globally, and Retimer shipments grew significantly in H1 2026, mainly Gen 5. The production version of its PCIe 6.x/CXL 3.x Retimer has taped out, is in customer test and validation, and was recently added to the PCI-SIG vendor list; per industry information, standard server CPUs supporting PCIe 6.x Retimers are expected to ship in volume next year. Management says some memory makers dropping in-house MXC chips for third-party parts reflects a return to specialization and means a larger market for third-party MXC vendors; industry analysis cited by management sees 2027 as the first year of CXL scale commercial use.
quarterly_data.figure: PCIe 5.0 Retimer: one of two main suppliers; PCIe 6.x/CXL 3.x Retimer production version taped out

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): the Q2 2026 change in interconnect-chip gross margin was mainly product mix, with lower-margin products growing faster. Short term, a rising share of new-sub-generation DDR5 RCDs helps margin, while rising industry demand will put some pressure on the supply side; over the medium to long term management expects interconnect-chip gross margin to stay at a relatively high level through sub-generation upgrades and new products.

Management (IR record): Q2 2026 revenue from the four new interconnect products was broadly stable versus Q1; for H2, demand for new products still in industry trial is uncertain and volume ramp depends on the ecosystem maturing. H1 2026 R&D expense was RMB 4.53 hundred million, up 26.9%, 13.6% of revenue, and management expects absolute R&D expense to keep growing as projects multiply.
quarterly_data.figure: H1 2026 R&D RMB 4.53 hundred million (+26.9%, 13.6% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): H2 2026 R&D plan is to tape out engineering samples of the PCIe 7.0 Retimer, PCIe Switch and high-speed Ethernet PHY Retimer chips, finish mass-production versions of the first and second batches of clock-buffer chips, and tape out a high-precision RTC engineering sample. H1 2026 milestones: sixth-sub-generation DDR5 RCD sampled, third-generation MRCD/MDB engineering samples taped out, PCIe 6.x/CXL 3.x Retimer and CXL 3.x MXC mass-production versions taped out. The Ethernet PHY Retimer, the first announced product in its Ethernet and optical-interconnect push, targets signal integrity between AI servers and switches.
quarterly_data.figure: PCIe 7.0 Retimer, PCIe Switch and Ethernet PHY Retimer engineering-sample tape-outs planned in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record), citing industry analysis: AI workloads shifting to inference and agents raise the CPU-to-GPU ratio in AI servers; a typical AI server CPU carries about 2 times the memory modules of a general-purpose server, and next-generation CPUs may raise memory channels from 8 or 12 to 16, lifting memory-interconnect chip volume. Rising MRDIMM use (1 MRCD + 10 MDB per module) would further expand the market versus a single RCD per RDIMM.
quarterly_data.figure: about 2x memory modules per CPU in AI servers; channels 8 or 12 to 16

quarterly_data.signal: Management (IR record): the company's clock chips shipped in H1 2026 were mainly clock generators and clock buffers for eSSD, data-center servers and industrial control, and it has received mass-production orders for these products; a high-precision RTC chip is expected to reach engineering-sample tape-out in H2.

contracts.signal: Management (IR record): in July 2026 Montage began trial production of its CXL 3.2 MXC chip (up to 64GT/s CXL and 8000MT/s DDR data rates), which has been designed into the next-generation CXL products of major memory-module makers including Samsung and SK Hynix.
